content: Cefixime, marketed under the brand name Suprax, is a cephalosporin-class antibacterial drug. Its use is specifically indicated for the treatment of infections in adults and pediatric patients aged six months or older, provided these infections are caused by susceptible bacterial strains. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to preserve the efficacy of Suprax and other antibacterial agents, it should only be used to treat infections that are either confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or modification of antimicrobial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns may inform empirical therapy decisions. The specific infections for which Suprax is indicated include: 1. Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Suprax is effective in treating uncomplicated UTIs caused by Escherichia coli and Proteus mirabilis. 2. Otitis Media: Suprax is indicated for the treatment of otitis media caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Streptococcus pyogenes. However, it is important to note that the efficacy of Suprax against Streptococcus pyogenes in this context was studied in fewer than 10 infections. Additionally, for otitis media caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, the overall response rate to cefixime was approximately 10% lower compared to the comparator drug. 3. Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis: Suprax is used to treat pharyngitis and tonsillitis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. However, penicillin remains the standard drug of choice for treating infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. While Suprax is generally effective in eradicating Streptococcus pyogenes from the nasopharynx, there is no available data to confirm its efficacy in preventing subsequent rheumatic fever. 4. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Suprax is indicated for the treatment of acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. 5. Uncomplicated Gonorrhea (Cervical/Urethral): Suprax is effective in treating uncomplicated gonorrhea (both cervical and urethral) caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, including both penicillinase-producing and non-penicillinase-producing strains. These indications highlight the importance of using Suprax judiciously and in accordance with susceptibility data to ensure its continued effectiveness in combating bacterial infections.
